title: Sandridge Road / Lake Asbury / First Coast Expressway land & development activity
description: District 5's Lake Asbury area is undergoing rapid change: the county-funded Sandridge Road (CR 739B) widening ($31.6M, per the county's own project page), a 2005 Lake Asbury Master Plan, a 2021 moratorium on new rezoning within the master-plan area, growth pressure tied to the First Coast Expressway, and a 2025 inter-neighborhood "connectivity" rezoning-adjacent plan that was withdrawn after public opposition. The lead is whether specific land sales, rezonings, or comprehensive-plan amendments in this corridor show a pattern connecting county infrastructure spending, private landowners/developers, and BCC/District 5 decisions.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief), refined against initial search research 2026-09-11.
entitiesInvolved: Clay County Public Works / Bonded Transportation Program
whyItMatters: Road-widening and rezoning decisions directly affect adjacent land values; if any BCC vote or land-use approval in this corridor coincided with a documented financial or personal relationship, that intersection would be a Voting-Conflict/Ethics lead, not by itself an allegation.
evidenceAvailable: Official county project page for the Sandridge Road widening (source: county Bonded Transportation Program). News coverage of the 2025 connectivity-plan withdrawal and general Lake Asbury growth pressure (secondary). Burke's own residence (Russell Landing, near Lake Asbury) is in this general area per her campaign bio (EV-024) — a mundane explanation for a small cluster of Sandridge-Road-area campaign donors (Sue Campbell 2020, Stu Opferman and Mike Elliott 2023) that does not require a developer-benefit theory. See COUNTER_EVIDENCE.md.
evidenceMissing: No parcel-level ownership chain (property appraiser → seller → buyer → LLC) has been built. No specific rezoning/comprehensive-plan-amendment case tied to this corridor has been pulled from BCC agendas/minutes. No confirmation of Burke's specific votes on any Lake Asbury/Sandridge-corridor item.
recordsNeeded: Clay County Property Appraiser parcel records for land adjacent to the Sandridge Road corridor
BCC agenda/minutes for all Lake Asbury Master Plan amendments and rezonings, 2019-present
The withdrawn 2025 "connectivity" plan application and who submitted it
Sunbiz records for any LLC that acquired land in this corridor during the widening project

title: Gustafson family / company connections to Clay County land and development matters
description: RESOLVED (core facts) 2026-09-11 via primary source: on June 24, 2025 the BCC denied (4-1) Sheryl Edlyn Gustafson's request (COMP 25-0010 / ZON 25-0007) to change 13.86 acres at 2005 S CR 16-A, Green Cove Springs (The Springs planning district, District 5) from Agriculture to Rural Residential/AR, despite staff, the Planning Commission (6-0), and the Springs Citizens Advisory Committee (6-0) all recommending approval. Vice-Chairman Kristen Burke personally made the motion to deny; Commissioner John Sgromolo seconded; Commissioner Jim Renninger was the lone dissenting vote (opposed to the denial). The property is Gustafson's own homesteaded residence since 2013, acquired via nominal-consideration family/trust transfers in 2012, not a recent outside-developer acquisition. NOTE: this parcel (CR 16-A / The Springs) is geographically distinct from the Sandridge Road / Lake Asbury corridor in LEAD-sandridge — do not conflate the two areas. Whether there is any broader Gustafson family/company footprint in Clay County beyond this one case remains open.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Core facts verified against official BCC minutes and Property Appraiser records 2026-09-11.
whyItMatters: This is now the investigation's best-documented single BCC action involving Burke: a motion she personally made, against staff/CAC/Planning-Commission recommendations, in her own district. Recorded neutrally — voting/moving against a staff recommendation is a normal, lawful exercise of a commissioner's discretion, not evidence of impropriety by itself. Whether there is a broader Gustafson pattern (beyond this one homesteaded family parcel) remains the open question.
evidenceAvailable: Official, e-signed BCC minutes (PrimeGov meetingTemplateId 8164) with full case detail, motion/second/vote, and a video timestamp (1:56:56-2:20:20). Official Property Appraiser parcel record (16-06-26-015574-001-02) with ownership and sale history back to 2012. The original CitizenPortal.ai lead is now confirmed partially accurate (topline facts) and partially wrong (commissioner names) — see EV-004/EV-010/EV-011/EV-012.
evidenceMissing: No confirmation of any OTHER Gustafson-connected parcel, business, or BCC matter beyond this one case. G Bar Ranch LLC / G Bar Ranch South LLC (the 2012 grantor, likely a Gustafson-family ranching entity) has not been independently confirmed via Sunbiz. No re-application (PUD or reduced-density) has been filed or found yet, per Chairman Condon's suggestion at the hearing.
recordsNeeded: Sunbiz detail for G Bar Ranch LLC / G Bar Ranch South LLC to confirm the Gustafson-family ranching-entity connection
A general Clay County land-record and BCC-agenda name search for 'Gustafson' beyond this one case, to establish or rule out a broader footprint
Any follow-up PUD or reduced-density re-application for this parcel

title: Burke chiropractic/business interests — including a reported newer clinic possibly involving a family member
description: Kristen Burke is a chiropractor and, per her practice's own site, has co-owned Fleming Island Family Chiropractic with her husband Harold Burke since 2000 — well-established, not in question. UPDATE 2026-09-11: Burke's own bio now confirms she has a brother and states the family "opened Oakleaf Family Chiropractic in 2009 for her brother and his family" — this is the first primary-source (self-published) confirmation of both the brother's existence and a specific named business. However, the Sunbiz corporate record for the matching entity name lists officers surnamed Thompson (Jeremy E. and Natalie), not Burke, and the practice's current public website shows unrelated doctors. This is now CONFLICTING EVIDENCE, not a blank slate — see PATTERN_MATRIX.md and COUNTER_EVIDENCE.md.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Major update 2026-09-11 via Burke's own bio + Sunbiz.
whyItMatters: If a Burke-family-connected business later sought or received a county permit, zoning approval, or other BCC action, that would be a Voting-Conflict/Ethics lead. Nothing found so far establishes that any such county action has occurred, even taking the family connection at face value.
evidenceAvailable: Self-published bio on Fleming Island Family Chiropractic's own website confirming Kristen + Harold Burke opened that practice in 2000, AND stating they opened Oakleaf Family Chiropractic in 2009 for her brother (EV-022). Oakleaf Family Chiropractic contributed $1,000 to Burke's campaign in BOTH the 2020 and 2023-2024 cycles (CAMPAIGN_REPEAT_DONORS.md). Fleming Island Family Chiropractic, Inc. confirmed active in Sunbiz (P00000100632). The Fleming Island practice donated $1,000 + $364.31 in-kind to Burke's own 2020 campaign and $500 in 2023 (EV-014). Campaign donor 'Kenneth Burke' ($100, 2020) is very likely Burke's own son (matches her stated child's name — EV-023), not an unknown relative. 'Laurie Burke' ($200, 2020) remains unmatched. A same-named 'Burke Chiropractic LLC' was found and DISPROVEN as connected (St. Petersburg, FL, owners James L. and Sarah E. Burke — EV-016).
evidenceMissing: Whether 'Jeremy Thompson' (the officer of record for the matching-named 2010 Oakleaf entity) is Burke's brother is NOT confirmed — her maiden name has not been established from a primary source. The second, currently-active 'Oakleaf Family Chiropractic, Inc.' entity (filed 2012) has not had its officers pulled. No permit, zoning, or BCC-action record tied to any of these businesses has been found.
recordsNeeded: Confirmation of Kristen Burke's maiden name from a primary source (marriage record, voter registration, or an interview/bio that states it directly) to test the Thompson hypothesis
Sunbiz officer detail for the second, active Oakleaf Family Chiropractic, Inc. entity (P12000019233)
Sunbiz officer/registered-agent detail for Fleming Island Family Chiropractic, Inc. (P00000100632)
Clay County / municipal business tax receipt and building-permit records for either chiropractic business

title: Stormwater assessment decision-making and Burke's role as Board Chair
description: RESOLVED (adoption vote) 2026-09-11 via primary source. The final Stormwater Utility and Assessment Ordinance was adopted July 28, 2026 by a unanimous 5-0 vote; Vice-Chairman John Sgromolo made both motions (ordinance and resolution), seconded by Jim Renninger. Chairman Kristen Burke chaired a calm hearing with a single speaker asking a cost question ($85/year confirmed). This is a materially different picture from the contentious hearings described in 2025 secondary news coverage, which appear to be earlier, separate meetings — see STORMWATER_MASTER_TIMELINE.md.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Adoption vote confirmed via primary source 2026-09-11.
whyItMatters: Establishes the factual public record of how the assessment was adopted and how the Board Chair conducted the process. The primary record of the actual enacting vote does not support a narrative of Burke personally pushing through an unpopular measure over strong opposition at that meeting — see COUNTER_EVIDENCE.md.
evidenceAvailable: Official BCC minutes for the July 28, 2026 adoption vote (EV-020), with video timestamp. Multiple secondary news accounts (Action News Jax, WOKV) of earlier, separate hearings and Burke's reported conduct as chair at those. Official county business-impact estimate already in ClayMoneyTrail's money dataset.
evidenceMissing: The specific date(s) and primary-source minutes for the earlier, contentious hearing(s) described in secondary coverage have not been identified. The hardship/veteran exemption vote specifically was not found in the July 28, 2026 minutes — it likely happened at an earlier meeting not yet pulled. No confirmation of where stormwater revenue is actually being spent (vs. budgeted) — the fee only took effect October 1, 2026.
recordsNeeded: Primary-source minutes for the earlier stormwater hearing(s) described by Action News Jax/WOKV, including the hardship/veteran exemption vote
Initial consultant contracts and staff studies preceding the ordinance
Actual (not budgeted) stormwater collections and expenditures once available (not yet possible — fee effective 2026-10-01)

title: Commissioner compensation increase proposal
description: Clay County commissioner salary has been fixed at $37,000/year since 2008 per the Home Rule Charter (already documented in ClayMoneyTrail's main dataset, sourceId: county-charter). UPDATE 2026-09-11: the Charter Review Commission approved final ballot language on 2026-03-16 to tie commissioner pay to Florida Statute 145.031 (raising it to over $100,000, described as tripling current pay — reconciling the earlier conflicting $60,000-vs-triple figures; $60,000 was an earlier/superseded draft). Public hearings followed April-May 2026. Measure pending for the November 2026 ballot. Whether Burke has personally advocated for or against it remains unestablished.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Ballot language and timeline confirmed 2026-09-11 (secondary source); Burke's position still not established.
whyItMatters: The mission brief explicitly warns not to attribute this proposal to Burke unless records establish that. No source found in either pass connects her to it in any way — see COUNTER_EVIDENCE.md.
evidenceAvailable: Secondary news coverage (Clay Views) with a specific date (2026-03-16), specific ballot language (tying pay to FS 145.031), and a public-hearing schedule. NovusAgenda agenda URLs located for two of the three hearings (MeetingID 2161, 2166) but not opened.
evidenceMissing: Primary Charter Review Commission minutes for the March 16 vote and three hearings not directly opened. No statement or vote by Burke found. Whether the BCC's forwarding role involves any actual vote (vs. a ministerial pass-through) is unconfirmed.
recordsNeeded: Primary Charter Review Commission minutes/video for the 2026-03-16 vote and the three public hearings
Confirmation of whether the BCC took any recorded vote to forward the ballot language
Any recorded statement by Burke specifically on this proposal, if one exists
